title: Time as nested modules
opening: You give yourself a week to see a result that takes two weeks to appear. Changing the deadline does not make the result happen sooner. The work you do today still needs to serve the larger pursuit.

labels.timelineIntro: Edit one horizon at a time. Mark dates imposed by real conditions separately from schedules chosen for coordination.
labels.realDate: A date or lead time set by a real condition
labels.dependency: Prerequisite, parallel work, lead time, compounding, decay, or irreversibility
labels.feedback: What evidence should arrive before commitment grows?
labels.comparison: When the schedule is shorter than the real lead time
labels.comparisonIntro: Illustrative values only. Move either date to see whether the chosen schedule leaves time for the effect to appear. A shorter chosen date cannot remove a biological or logistical lead time.
labels.gap: The chosen schedule ends before the effect can be observed. Change the process, coordinate around the real lead time, or accept bounded uncertainty.
labels.fits: The chosen schedule includes the stated lead time. It still needs feedback and evidence to fit the process.
labels.practice: Plan nested time for a real pursuit
labels.practiceIntro: Identify one real deadline and one chosen schedule. Include dependencies, feedback, and the larger direction.
labels.private: This private note is optional. The six required course questions are separate.
labels.length: This full note is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote: First ask which dates come from real conditions and which you have imposed. A chosen schedule can support a pursuit; an inherited one can crowd out curiosity without serving the outcome. Removing artificial pressure leaves room to follow a question, while lifespan, resources and other real limits still matter.
labels.responseContinue: Continue while current evidence and dependencies still support the chosen timing.
labels.responseChange: Change the timing or method to fit the observed dependency.
labels.responseStop: Stop this schedule while the chosen outcome or its conditions are reconsidered.
labels.responseRecover: Recover by restoring the resources or conditions needed to continue.

feedback.unavailable: Private saving is unavailable. Your note stays on screen.
feedback.length: Shorten the full note to fit the 2,000-character limit. Your text stays here.
feedback.conflict: This note changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here; compare the saved version before saving again.
feedback.readFailure: The saved note could not be loaded.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same note before changing it.

example.pursuit: A source inspection can finish today, while an external response remains pending.
example.real: The outside response has not arrived. The waiting time is not controlled by the inspection schedule.
example.chosen: Complete independent research this week; review the decision when the response arrives.
example.dependencies: Independent reading can proceed in parallel. A decision that requires the response depends on it.
example.return: Check the response before deciding. If its arrival changes the bottleneck, revise the next horizon.
